title: A Call to Scattered Israel
summary: A speaker calls to scattered Israel and says the Lord called him from the womb and made mention of his name.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker addresses the house of Israel, including those scattered abroad and people from far away.
The Lord called the speaker from the womb and made mention of his name before birth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The address can be presented as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity, appearance, age, and physical location are not stated.
No listeners or visible people are specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Hearken, O ye house of Israel,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The speaker

narration.text: the Lord hath called me from the womb;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chapter is presented as prophetic speech; its metaphors should not be visualized as literal events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a birth or identify the speaker as a particular person.

title: The Servant's Calling
summary: The speaker describes the Lord's protection and calling using images of a sharp sword, a polished shaft, and a quiver.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says the Lord made his mouth like a sharp sword, hid him in the shadow of the Lord's hand, and made him a polished shaft hidden in a quiver.
The Lord calls the speaker his servant, Israel, in whom he will be glorified.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the words as off-screen speech; the sword, shaft, hand, and quiver are metaphors, not narrated visible events.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance are not stated.
The Lord's visible appearance is not described.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage uses figurative language; do not depict its metaphors as literal supernatural actions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible Lord, weapon, quiver, or act of hiding as a literal event.

title: The Speaker's Doubt

title: Strength and Glory
summary: The Lord says the servant will bring Jacob back, restore Israel, and be a light to the Gentiles and salvation to the ends of the earth.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord formed the speaker from the womb to be his servant and bring Jacob back to him; though Israel is not gathered, the speaker will be glorious in the Lord's eyes, and God will be his strength.
The Lord says the servant will raise up Jacob's tribes, restore Israel's preserved people, and be a light to the Gentiles and salvation to the ends of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen speech; the text does not narrate the restoration as taking place in this moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance, and the appearance of the Lord, are unstated.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jacob, Israel, or the Gentiles being gathered as a current event.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord addresses one despised by people, abhorred by a nation, and servant of rulers; kings will see and arise, and princes will worship because the Lord is faithful.

title: A Covenant and a Way Home
summary: The Lord says he has helped and preserved the addressed people, giving his servant as a covenant and promising release to prisoners and provision in high places.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he heard and helped the isles of the sea, will preserve them, and give his servant as a covenant of the people to establish the earth and enable inheritance of desolate heritages.
The servant is to tell prisoners to go forth and those in darkness to show themselves; they will feed along the ways and find pasture in high places.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen speech rather than showing the promised release or journey as current events.

explicit_facts.text: The people will not hunger or thirst, nor be struck by heat or sun; the merciful one will lead and guide them by springs of water.
The Lord will make all his mountains a way and exalt his highways.

title: Gathering from Afar

explicit_facts.text: People will come from far away, from the north and west, and from the land of Sinim.
Heaven, earth, and mountains are called to sing and rejoice because the Lord has comforted his people and will have mercy on the afflicted.

title: Zion's Fear Answered
summary: Zion says the Lord has forsaken and forgotten her; the Lord answers that he will not forget the house of Israel, even if a mother could forget her child.

explicit_facts.text: Zion says the Lord has forsaken and forgotten her, but he will show that he has not.
The Lord asks whether a woman can forget her nursing child and says that even if they may forget, he will not forget the house of Israel.
